terms.definition: A concise representation of a document’s content.
The process of preparing abstracts.
Indexing in which an indexer selects terms from an indexing language or controlled vocabulary, rather than copying them directly from the document.
An abstract prepared by the author of the original document.
Indexing performed by computer algorithms with little or no manual intervention.
Broader Term; a more general concept within a thesaurus hierarchy.
An alphabetical guide to the significant content of a book, with locators, usually placed at the end.
Current Awareness Service.
A pre-coordinate indexing technique, associated with S. R. Ranganathan, that derives subject entries from the hierarchical chain of a classification scheme.
The use of software to support tasks such as sorting, formatting, and cross-reference management, while the indexer retains intellectual control.
An organised set of authorised terms used consistently for indexing and retrieval.
An abstract that summarises a document while also offering an evaluation of its strengths, weaknesses, or significance.
A See or See also note directing a reader from one index term to another.
A technique that varies the leading term in a compound subject to create multiple access points.
Indexing based on features taken directly from the document, such as title words.
A digital index that updates automatically when the underlying document changes.
The extent to which important document concepts are represented in indexing.
The proportion of non-relevant documents retrieved, out of all non-relevant documents available.
A digital index whose entries link directly to the relevant section of a document.
A systematically arranged guide to the contents of a document, consisting of terms and locators.
Representing document content with terms or symbols to support retrieval.
A database or publication, such as Scopus or MEDLINE, that provides organised indexing and abstracting access to literature across a discipline.
An abstract that indicates the scope or topics covered by a document.
An abstract that reports substantive content such as purpose, method, findings, and conclusion.
International and British standards providing guidance on the content, structure, and preparation of indexes.
Keyword in Context.
Keyword Out of Context.
The page, section, or paragraph reference attached to an index entry.
Narrower Term; a more specific concept within a thesaurus hierarchy.
Indexing in which concepts are combined during retrieval.
Preserved Context Index System, developed by Derek Austin.
The proportion of retrieved documents that are relevant.
Indexing in which concepts are combined before retrieval.
The proportion of all relevant documents that are actually retrieved.
Related Term; an associated concept that is neither equivalent nor hierarchical.
Selective Dissemination of Information.
Selective Listing in Combination.
The precision with which an indexing term represents a concept.
The intellectual examination of a document to identify its subject content.
A controlled vocabulary organised by defined semantic relationships.
Used For; a reference from a preferred term to a non-preferred term.
A reference directing a non-preferred term to the preferred term.
